title: How a Goatherd Became a Prophet: The Life of Muhammad
description:
Over 1,400 years ago, in the bustling trade hub of Mecca, a goatherd named Muhammad ibn Abdullah rose to become the prophet of a new faith: Islam. But was this divine destiny or the story of a man who turned tales of yesteryears into revelations?

In this documentary, Pale Blue Thoughts traces the life and rise of Muhammad. From his early orphanhood in the Quraysh tribe, to his marriage with Khadija, to his first visions in the Cave of Hira, we unpack the origins of Islam. We examine how Khadija and her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal helped frame Muhammad’s encounters as divine, how the Quran was compiled in a non-chronological and inconsistent order, and how early followers used superstition to confirm his prophethood.

We follow Muhammad through 13 years of failed conversions in Mecca, the Hijra to Medina, the raids and battles (including the Battle of Badr), and finally the conquest of Mecca in 630 CE. Along the way, we debunk the myths of Isra and Mi’raj (the night journey on Buraaq), expose the destruction of 360 idols in the Kaaba, and highlight how Islam grew from a small cult to a political-military empire.

If you’ve searched for Muhammad biography explained, Quran history debunked, Cave of Hira revelation, origins of Islam, Prophet Muhammad exposed, or conquest of Mecca, this video gives you the evidence-based perspective.

#MuhammadExposed #OriginsOfIslam #CriticalThinking #ScienceOverSuperstition #QuranDebunked

Don’t forget to subscribe, like, comment, and share — hype this video so it reaches more people and sparks better conversations!

00:00 Intro — Mecca before Muhammad
01:10 Childhood, Khadija & the Cave of Hira
02:40 The first revelations & Quran’s contradictions
04:00 From Mecca to Medina: Hijra, raids & battles
05:30 The conquest of Mecca & destruction of idols
06:50 Conclusion — Muhammad’s legacy of faith & power

The idea that early Muslims defecated on idols during the Meccan period of Islam is not supported by authentic historical sources. The early Muslims, including the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), were known for their respectful and dignified conduct, even in the face of opposition from the Quraysh and other idol-worshippers in Mecca.

Islam advocates for treating others with respect, even when disagreeing with their beliefs. The Quran emphasizes that Muslims should not insult the deities of others to avoid reciprocal disrespect (Quran 6:108):

"And do not insult those they invoke besides Allah, lest they insult Allah in enmity without knowledge."

While early Muslims did reject idol worship and sought to convey the message of monotheism, the historical records indicate that they engaged in peaceful preaching, rather than acts of disrespect or desecration, even under persecution. If you're encountering claims like these, they may stem from misinterpretations or unreliable sources.
